pod.description: Claim analysis: reducing the power of the powerful is usually a net benefit; revised premise: no actor can ensure even distribution of power, because relinquishing power removes the capacity to guarantee the outcome

words.name: power reduction claim
words.description: reducing the power of powerful actors is usually a net benefit, not a harm

words.name: distribution impossibility premise
words.description: no actor can ensure even distribution of power: the act of relinquishing power removes the capacity to guarantee the distribution's outcome

words.name: self-undermining transfer
words.description: logical structure in which executing the transfer destroys the enforcement capacity for the transfer's goal

words.name: boeckenfoerde dilemma
words.description: the liberal state lives on preconditions it cannot itself guarantee; static analogue of the premise

words.name: self-enforcing equilibrium
words.description: even distribution can persist only as a coordination equilibrium among many actors, not as a guaranteed state

words.name: power reconcentration
words.description: distributed power tends to reconcentrate over time (iron law of oligarchy)

words.name: continuous reduction strategy
words.description: because even distribution is neither achievable in one act nor stable, ongoing marginal reduction of concentrated power is the second-best strategy

words.name: power vacuum risk
words.description: abrupt power reduction can transfer power to worse actors instead of counterweights

words.name: historical transition failure
words.description: post-abdication collapse cases: Sulla's restored republic, Diocletian's tetrarchy

values.description: probability that no single actor can guarantee even power distribution, given the self-undermining structure of the transfer
probability that marginal reduction of concentrated power toward counterweights yields net benefit; raised from 0.7 in v0.0.1 because the revised premise supports the second-best argument
probability that distributed power reconcentrates absent active counterbalancing
probability that the Sulla and Diocletian cases show abdication without outcome guarantee

sources.name: Boeckenfoerde 1967
sources.description: Die Entstehung des Staates als Vorgang der Saekularisation, source of the Boeckenfoerde dilemma

sources.name: Weingast 1997
sources.description: The Political Foundations of Democracy and the Rule of Law, American Political Science Review 91(2), constitutions as self-enforcing coordination equilibria

sources.name: Michels 1911
sources.description: Zur Soziologie des Parteiwesens, iron law of oligarchy
